skim: Typhoon Dolphin bears down on China’s Zhejiang coast as emergency crews evacuate fishing fleets, all 14 missing in Washington’s Spokane-area fires were located as Oregon shattered its all-time wildfire acreage record, Greece arrested 33 people over the Athens-area blaze, DR Congo’s Ebola death toll passed 1,580 as the region’s largest treatment center opened, and nearly 80,000 Kumamoto households remain without water.

A Strait of Hormuz deal remains unsigned as Iran’s leadership withholds final approval, Netanyahu publicly broke with the White House over its Gaza draft — “We did not agree. It is not our draft” — a Russian barrage killed 17 in Kyiv as Zelenskyy pleaded for interceptors, Venezuela’s transition talks opened shakily without Machado, and Israel struck Lebanon again as Rome talks hit round seven.

AstraZeneca shares rebounded 6% after a source denied any Bristol Myers merger talks ever existed, the Dow topped 54,000 and the S&P 500 hit a fresh record, SpaceX’s debut public earnings showed 92% revenue growth overshadowed by heavy AI capex, and AMD’s record data-center quarter was overshadowed by capex worries.

The White House met OpenAI, Anthropic, Google and Meta on a new AI safety framework — then refused to release any details, drawing a ‘baffling’ rebuke that “we can’t have secret, voluntary rules” — as the EU activated AI Act enforcement powers against the same three labs, OpenAI reabsorbed Lilian Weng from Thinking Machines, and Anthropic began building its own AI chip team.

Kashmir marked the Article 370 anniversary under heavy guard as Modi hailed a ‘decisive new chapter,’ Bihar’s NDA kept huddling after its Bankipur bypoll shock, Apple filed a fresh UK legal challenge over an iCloud backdoor order as Reform UK’s navy plan was mocked over a ship photo blunder, and Qatar reaffirmed its Hormuz mediator role as the Amir spoke with Trump by phone.

stories.headline: Typhoon Dolphin Set To Slam Zhejiang Coast As China Activates Emergency Response
stories.body: Typhoon Dolphin is forecast to make landfall along the coast of China’s Zhejiang province “between Sunday night and Monday morning as a typhoon or severe typhoon,” per Global Times (Aug 6), with Shanghai, Zhejiang and Fujian all activating emergency response protocols. Fujian has already completed evacuating all fishing vessels from designated fishing grounds, while Zhejiang ordered personnel off offshore aquaculture and construction sites as the storm bears down on a region already reeling from weeks of flooding.

stories.headline: All 14 Missing Located In Washington Fires; Oregon Sets All-Time Wildfire Acreage Record
stories.body: All 14 people previously unaccounted for in the Spokane-area wildfires have now been reached by authorities, per Northwest News Network (Aug 4), as the blazes — which have burned over 8,000 acres, destroyed 700–1,100 structures and forced more than 65,000 evacuations — continue to burn with zero to 13% containment. Aaron Farinacci, 37, a convicted felon, has been charged with “knowingly and maliciously” starting the largest of the fires, the Old Trails Fire, while further south Oregon has already topped 2 million acres burned this season, breaking its 2024 annual record just three days into August, per The Spokesman-Review (Aug 3).

stories.headline: Athens-Area Wildfire Brought Under Control After Burning 14,000 Hectares; 33 Arrested
stories.body: The wildfire northwest of Athens is now largely contained after tearing through more than 14,000 hectares over five days, with a fire service spokesperson saying “the situation in the region is much better,” though crews remain “on maximum alert” for flare-ups, per Euronews (Aug 5). Greek authorities have arrested 33 people since June 29 — 30 for negligence and three on arson suspicion — as the fire’s death toll stands at five, including the two helicopter crew members killed in a mid-air collision while dropping water on the blaze.

stories.headline: DR Congo Ebola Death Toll Passes 1,580 As Region’s Largest Treatment Center Opens
stories.body: The Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has reached 3,605 confirmed cases and 1,587 deaths across five provinces, with Ituri province alone accounting for 88% of cases, per UN News (Aug 3). The International Medical Corps is opening the country’s largest Ebola treatment facility this week — 100 beds, plus a transit center at the Kigonze displacement camp in Bunia — as WFP’s Carl Skau warned: “Ebola is moving fast, hitting people already facing conflict and hunger. Communities are key to ending it, but need support.”

stories.headline: Kumamoto Quake Toll Hits 38 As Nearly 80,000 Homes Remain Without Water
stories.body: The death toll from Japan’s magnitude-7.1 Kumamoto earthquake has risen to 38, including victims still being confirmed as quake-related, per Nippon.com (Aug 2). Roughly 79,700 households remain without running water more than a week after the quake, with officials saying there is “currently no timetable for restoring water service” to the hardest-hit municipalities.

stories.headline: Pakistan Level Series with Eight-Wicket Trinidad Win
stories.body: Abdullah Shafique’s unbeaten 160 in the first innings, backed by a four-wicket burst from Sajid Khan, powered Pakistan to an eight-wicket win over West Indies at Queen’s Park Oval, levelling the two-match series 1-1 after their 90-run defeat in the opener, per Pakistan Today (Aug 5). Shafique remained unbeaten again in the chase on 24 alongside Babar Azam as Pakistan completed a rare overseas Test win built on spin. West Indies bowling coach Ravi Rampaul credited Jomel Warrican’s resistance but conceded Pakistan’s spin attack had turned the match.

stories.headline: Kashmir’s Auqib Nabi Handed Maiden India Test Call-Up
stories.body: The BCCI has confirmed Shubman Gill will captain a 15-man India squad for the two-Test tour of Sri Lanka (Galle, Aug 15-19; Colombo, Aug 23-27), with KL Rahul as vice-captain, per Business Standard (Aug 3). Jammu & Kashmir seamer Auqib Nabi, 29 — who took 104 wickets across the last two Ranji Trophy seasons and helped J&K to a maiden Ranji title — earns a maiden call-up as cover for the injured Jasprit Bumrah, becoming the first Kashmir valley player picked for India’s Test side; the BCCI called him “Bumrah’s replacement” in its release. Off-spinner Saransh Jain, 33, also gets a first call after six wickets and 70 runs on India A’s recent Sri Lanka tour.

stories.headline: Juventus ‘Ready to Strike’ Zirkzee Loan Deal
stories.body: Manchester United and Juventus are locked in talks over Joshua Zirkzee, with Sky Italia’s Gianluca Di Marzio reporting the clubs are “ready to strike” and that the English club has already opened to a loan, per UtdReport (Aug 5). United want a loan with an obligation to buy rather than an option, while journalist Matteo Moretto says Zirkzee is “awaiting clarity” on the terms; the striker made just 24 Premier League appearances and 609 minutes last season and wants regular football with Marcus Rashford’s return squeezing his opportunities.

stories.headline: Ter Stegen Joins Ajax on Loan to Chase Klopp’s Eye
stories.body: Barcelona goalkeeper Marc-André ter Stegen, 34, has completed a season-long loan to Ajax under new coach Míchel Sánchez, aiming to force his way back into Germany’s plans under incoming national coach Jürgen Klopp after missing this summer’s World Cup, per the Washington Post (Aug 4). Ajax technical director Jordi Cruijff welcomed the move, saying “Marc has an outstanding track record, and his qualities are widely recognized,” with the veteran shot-stopper arriving after an earlier loan spell at Girona this year.

stories.headline: Verstappen Urged to Stay Put as Red Bull Future Speculation Builds
stories.body: With Red Bull winless and off the championship pace this season, former F1 driver Juan Pablo Montoya urged Max Verstappen to resist any temptation to leave: “I don’t think Max wants to leave Red Bull… You’re in the right place,” he said, per Yahoo Sports (Aug 5). The comments come as ex-driver Robert Doornbos predicts Verstappen — contracted through 2028 but holding an exit clause — will use the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort to clarify his future, per GPFans, with the team keen to “focus entirely on 2027” regardless of his decision.

stories.headline: AstraZeneca Rebounds as Source Denies $400bn Bristol Myers Merger Talks
stories.body: A senior source told Reuters “There is no deal between AstraZeneca and BMS. There never was a deal to be done, and there are no discussions between the companies,” per Investing.com (Aug 5), sending AstraZeneca shares surging roughly 6% and clawing back most of the 7% slide triggered by weekend reports of a prospective $400bn megamerger. Bristol Myers Squibb, which had jumped 6% on the original report, gave back some of those gains as the denial cooled speculation about a tie-up analysts warned would face heavy antitrust scrutiny given the two firms’ overlapping oncology pipelines.

stories.headline: Dow Tops 54,000, S&P 500 Hits Fresh Record on Earnings Strength
stories.body: Wall Street extended its rally into a fifth straight session on Wednesday, with the Dow surging over 900 points to a record close above 54,000 and the S&P 500 closing above 7,700 for the first time, per CNN Business (Aug 4); by Wednesday morning the S&P had touched a fresh intraday high of 7,793.68 while the Dow added another 456 points, per TheStreet (Aug 5). Analysts credited “easing geopolitical risks, strong earnings growth” and diplomatic progress around the Strait of Hormuz, even as WTI crude ticked up 0.75% to $76.34 a barrel and Brent rose 1.56% to $79.82.

stories.headline: SpaceX Stock Slumps 20% Below IPO Price Despite 92% Revenue Jump
stories.body: In its first-ever public earnings report, SpaceX posted Q2 revenue of $7.8bn, up 92% year-over-year from $4.7bn in Q1 and delivering $3.5bn in adjusted EBITDA, per KuCoin News (Aug 4). CFO Bret Johnsen pointed to surging “AI compute agreements” as a key margin driver, but the stock still fell more than 20% below its $135 IPO price as investors balked at heavy capital spending, with shares whipsawing as much as 8% lower intraday according to TradingKey (Aug 4).

stories.headline: AMD Shares Sink 8% Even as Data-Center Revenue More Than Doubles
stories.body: AMD posted record Q2 revenue of $11.5bn, up 50% year-over-year, with data-center sales more than doubling to $6.7bn — now 58% of total revenue — per Yahoo Finance (Aug 4). CEO Lisa Su said “we delivered an excellent quarter, with record revenue and profitability as Data Center revenue more than doubled year-over-year,” and the company guided Q3 revenue to $12.7–13.3bn, but shares still fell more than 8% in after-hours trading as investors fretted over rising capex and margin pressure.

stories.headline: Disney Beats on Parks and Streaming, Lifts Buyback Target to $9bn
stories.body: Disney posted Q3 2026 revenue of $25.2bn (up 7%) and adjusted EPS of $2.06, beating the $1.86 analyst estimate as adjusted net income jumped 23% to $3.8bn, per The Motley Fool (Aug 5). The Experiences division led the way at nearly $10bn (up 10%) on theme-park price increases and a travel boom, while Entertainment revenue rose 6% to $11.3bn; Disney also raised its fiscal 2026 buyback target to $9bn — up from $8bn last quarter — and reaffirmed 12–16% adjusted EPS growth guidance for the year.

stories.headline: White House Keeps New AI Safety Framework Under Wraps After Meeting Tech Giants
stories.body: Meta, Nvidia, Microsoft, OpenAI, Anthropic and other firms met White House officials on Aug 4 in Washington to review a draft framework for evaluating frontier AI models before release — but the administration confirmed it won’t publish the details, calling participation voluntary and keeping the process known only to select companies, per Fortune (Aug 4). The secrecy drew sharp criticism; the Council on Foreign Relations’ Chris McGuire called it ‘baffling,’ saying “we can’t have secret, voluntary rules to regulate the most important tech in the world.” The meeting followed the Hugging Face/PyPI hacking revelations that pushed cybersecurity and model-safety testing to the top of the agenda.

stories.headline: EU Activates AI Act Enforcement Powers Against OpenAI, Anthropic and Google
stories.body: Brussels formally activated new enforcement powers on Aug 2 that let the EU AI Office and national regulators fine companies up to €15 million or 3% of global annual turnover, whichever is higher, per Help Net Security (Aug 4). New transparency rules now require chatbots to identify themselves as automated systems, deepfakes to carry labels, and general-purpose AI providers to publish a ‘sufficiently detailed summary’ of training data and content. The move intensifies an already tense relationship between the European Commission and major U.S. AI labs just as Washington finalizes its own, less transparent framework.

stories.headline: Lilian Weng’s Reversal Underscores Escalating AI Talent War
stories.body: Thinking Machines co-founder Lilian Weng abruptly left the startup on Jul 29, telling colleagues in a message on X, “I don’t feel I’m able to continue at the pace a startup requires,” citing health strain — then rejoined OpenAI within days, per TechCrunch (Jul 29). She returns to lead a top-level research team on recursive self-improvement, the process of AI systems enhancing their own capabilities. Former colleague Mira Murati responded, “I’m glad that you’re putting your health first,” while the episode fuels ongoing scrutiny of the punishing pace at frontier labs poaching and re-poaching top researchers.

stories.headline: Nvidia Tracking Toward Jensen Huang’s $1 Trillion Blackwell-Rubin Bet
stories.body: Nvidia remains on pace for CEO Jensen Huang’s prediction of “at least $1 trillion” in Blackwell and Rubin chip demand visibility through 2027, with fiscal 2026 data center revenue at $194 billion and Wall Street penciling in $394 billion for 2026 and $561 billion for 2027, per The Motley Fool (Aug 2). Q1 fiscal 2027 data center revenue grew 92% year-over-year to $75 billion, and CFO Colette Kress reiterated “full confidence in the $1 trillion in Blackwell and Rubin revenue.” Risks remain from supply-chain execution and hyperscalers like Amazon and Google building competing custom chips.

stories.headline: Anthropic Builds Own Chip Team as Meta Compute-Lease Talks Continue
stories.body: Anthropic is assembling an in-house custom silicon team to co-design hardware alongside its Claude models “to help its technology run faster and more efficiently,” per TechCrunch (Aug 5), joining OpenAI’s Broadcom-built Jalapeno chip, Google’s TPUs and Meta’s MTIA in the race to escape Nvidia dependence; Anthropic has also explored Samsung as a manufacturing partner. The push comes as Anthropic remains in early talks to lease roughly $10 billion in compute from Meta over two years — about $417 million monthly — on top of its existing AWS, Google, Nvidia and AMD infrastructure and its $45 billion, three-year SpaceX deal for 220,000-plus GPUs.

stories.headline: Hormuz Deal Still Not Signed as Iran Awaits Leadership Sign-Off
stories.body: Trump said a Strait of Hormuz agreement could land “tomorrow or the next day,” but Iran’s foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said Tehran’s top leadership still has to approve it, cautioning that safe passage cannot be guaranteed “as long as the US maintained a naval blockade,” per Al Jazeera (Aug 5). The framework under discussion is a 60-day, fee-free arrangement with inbound tankers routed through Iranian waters and outbound traffic through Omani waters — Iran wants toll-collection rights as a coastal state, while Washington is holding out for “total freedom of commercial navigation” without Iranian approval.

stories.headline: Netanyahu Publicly Breaks With Trump Team Over Gaza Draft
stories.body: In a rare open rift with Washington, Netanyahu said of the US-drafted Gaza plan, “We did not agree. It is not our draft. We sent our comments,” and insisted “Israel will not withdraw from its current lines in Gaza until Hamas has completely disarmed,” per Euronews (Aug 4). He added he stands firm on Israel’s interests “both wisely and firmly,” leaving the Trump administration’s disarmament-first draft in limbo.

stories.headline: Kyiv Barrage Kills 17 as Zelenskyy Pleads for Interceptors
stories.body: Russia hit Kyiv overnight Tuesday with 24 ballistic missiles, 4 cruise missiles and 115 drones, killing at least 17 people and setting warehouses ablaze in Brovary and Bucha, per Al Jazeera (Aug 5). Zelenskyy said “ballistic missile interceptors could have saved the lives of those killed today,” warning that “delays in supplying them, or an unwillingness to provide anti-ballistic systems, lead directly to such horrific casualties and destruction” as Ukraine’s Patriot stockpile runs thin.

stories.headline: Venezuela’s PSUV-Opposition Talks Open Shakily, Without Machado
stories.body: Government negotiator Jorge Rodríguez and opposition counterpart Dinorah Figuera each announced a phone call launching “institutional dialogue” on earthquake response, democracy and political rights, with in-person talks set for Caracas next week, per Caracas Chronicles (Aug 3). María Corina Machado is staying out, saying she “will not join the talks nor block them” while demanding freed prisoners, exile returns and a firm election timeline before backing any deal.

stories.headline: Israel Strikes Lebanon Again as Rome Talks Hit Round Seven
stories.body: Israeli airstrikes killed one person and wounded 11 at a cemetery in Tebnine and forced evacuations in Al-Mansouri on Wednesday, with the IDF citing a Hezbollah ceasefire violation and warning residents to move “at least 1,000 meters away,” per the Denver Gazette (Aug 5). The strikes came as Israeli and Lebanese officials wrapped a seventh round of Rome peace talks, still deadlocked over Beirut’s demand for full Israeli withdrawal from the south versus Israel’s insistence on complete Hezbollah disarmament.

fixtures.headline: India Open Sri Lanka Tour Under New Test Captain Gill
fixtures.body: India begin their two-match Test series in Sri Lanka with the opener at Galle International Stadium, Shubman Gill’s first assignment as full-time Test captain, before the series wraps up at Colombo’s SSC.
fixtures.when: Aug 15-19 (1st Test, Galle); Aug 23-27 (2nd Test, Colombo)

fixtures.headline: Premier League 2026-27 Kicks Off with Arsenal-Coventry Opener
fixtures.body: Defending champions Arsenal host newly promoted Coventry City to open the new Premier League season, with Newcastle vs Liverpool, Manchester City vs Bournemouth and a Fulham-Chelsea derby also on the opening-weekend card.

fixtures.headline: F1 Returns from Summer Break at Zandvoort
fixtures.body: Formula 1 resumes after the summer shutdown with the Dutch Grand Prix at Zandvoort, a race some insiders expect Max Verstappen to use to settle speculation over his long-term future at Red Bull.

portfolio.headline: SpaceX Commits to Exclusive Nvidia GPU Buildout
portfolio.body: Nvidia rallied after SpaceX said on its earnings call that it will build its AI systems exclusively on Nvidia GPUs, with Elon Musk citing the Vera Rubin architecture as the deciding factor and pledging to take a significant share of Nvidia’s upcoming chip supply, per The Motley Fool (Aug 5). The commitment reinforces demand visibility for Nvidia’s next-generation Rubin platform heading into its ramp.

portfolio.headline: Alphabet Shaken by AI Leadership Shakeup, Antitrust Overhang
portfolio.body: Alphabet shares slid after news that DeepMind CEO Demis Hassabis is moving into an expanded chief scientist role — stepping back from the CEO-succession speculation that surrounded him — while longtime AI researcher Jeff Dean is departing to start his own venture, per AOL (Aug 5). Same-day coverage from TradingKey added that the move compounded existing investor worries about antitrust remedies tied to recent rulings against Alphabet and about margin pressure from heavy AI-infrastructure capex.

portfolio.headline: Figma Sinks Despite Beat-and-Raise Quarter
portfolio.body: Figma topped Wall Street estimates on both revenue and adjusted earnings and raised its full-year revenue guidance, with net dollar retention above 130% and strong growth in $10K+ and $100K+ ARR customers, per Benzinga (Aug 5). Even so, shares fell sharply in after-hours trading on heavy selling pressure, without a specific catalyst beyond the market digesting valuation after the post-IPO run.

portfolio.headline: Uber’s Bookings and Cash Flow Shine, but Revenue Narrowly Missed
portfolio.body: Uber’s Q2 2026 adjusted earnings per share edged past forecasts while revenue came in just short of estimates, but gross bookings grew more than 20% year-over-year for a fourth straight quarter and trailing twelve-month free cash flow topped $10 billion for the first time, per an Investing.com earnings-call transcript (Aug 5). Management also detailed an autonomous-vehicle push now live in seven cities with a target of fifteen by year-end, backed by a multibillion-dollar multi-year AV investment program.

portfolio.headline: Cloudflare Pulls Back Ahead of Today’s Earnings Report
portfolio.body: Cloudflare shares eased into Thursday’s session as investors positioned ahead of its Q2 2026 results, due after the market close today; analysts expect year-over-year revenue growth to accelerate from the prior quarter’s pace, per a StockStory preview (Aug 4). The stock had rallied sharply over the past month heading into the print and now trades well above the average Wall Street price target, leaving room for a give-back regardless of the report itself.

portfolio.headline: Fubo Posts Record Subscribers on World Cup, Disney Tie-Up
portfolio.body: Fubo’s Q2 2026 report showed record North American subscribers and narrower losses than a year ago, with CEO Alisa Bowen crediting major sporting events including the FIFA World Cup 2026 and improved advertising following its Disney integration, per Benzinga (Aug 5). Revenue fell just short of estimates, but the company raised its full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance and reaffirmed its 2028 profitability target.

portfolio.headline: Coeur Mining Posts Record Quarter, Starts First-Ever Dividend
portfolio.body: Coeur Mining reported record Q2 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA along with record gold production, driven by the first full quarter of contributions from its newly acquired New Afton and Rainy River mines plus stronger output at Wharf, per Junior Mining Network (Aug 5). The company also launched an enhanced capital-return program with its first-ever dividend and share buybacks, while trimming near-term guidance at the newly acquired mines to reflect a slower ramp-up; a conference call to discuss results is scheduled for today, Aug 6.

portfolio.headline: Hydrofarm Gives Back Part of Its Peat-Sale Spike
portfolio.body: Hydrofarm remains volatile as the market continues to digest this week’s sale of its Aurora Peat Products division to Raven Holdings, with proceeds earmarked to pay down the company’s term-loan debt as part of a new “Project Agility” pivot toward logistics and controlled-environment agriculture, per Timothy Sykes’ coverage (Aug 5). Today’s pullback follows the initial surge on that news and reflects the stock’s continued status as a high-risk, thinly capitalized turnaround story.

portfolio.headline: Fastly Margins Expand as Security Business Accelerates
portfolio.body: Fastly’s Q2 2026 revenue grew 23% year-over-year while gross margin expanded meaningfully as costs stayed roughly flat, with its security segment growing faster than the core network-services business and net retention hitting its highest level in over three years, per TradingKey’s summary of the company’s release (Aug 5). Fastly raised its full-year revenue guidance, though the report flagged rising customer concentration, with its top ten accounts now making up a larger share of revenue than a year ago.

stories.headline: Kashmir Marks Article 370 Anniversary Under Heavy Guard as Modi Hails ‘Decisive New Chapter’
stories.body: Seven years after Article 370’s abrogation, Jammu & Kashmir marked the anniversary under tight security following this month’s twin terror strikes, with PM Modi declaring the day “marked a decisive new chapter” for J&K and Ladakh, pointing to two new AIIMS campuses and over 1,100 annual medical seats (per Business Today, Aug 5). Per WION (Aug 4), the contrast with Pakistan-occupied Kashmir is stark — a doctor-to-population ratio of roughly 1:3,900 and more than 90 protest deaths there in the past two months. Security remains multi-layered across south Kashmir as forces hunt the Lashkar-linked TRF cell behind the Anantnag and Kulgam strikes.

stories.headline: Two More Karnataka Congress MLAs Quit as Shivakumar Downplays Cabinet Revolt
stories.body: Karnataka’s Congress crisis deepened as legislators Yashvantharayagouda V Patil and Belur Gopalakrishna resigned after being left out of Monday’s 19-minister cabinet expansion. Per The News Mill (Aug 4), Chief Minister D.K. Shivakumar shrugged off the departures, saying “resignations are a part of politics—no one can stop those who want to resign,” while recalling his own patience when once denied a berth. He has promised excluded members “appropriate responsibilities” and told ministers to focus on drought relief instead.

stories.headline: Nitish Kumar Huddles With Modi as NDA Reels From Bankipur Bypoll Shock
stories.body: A day after Jan Suraaj founder Prashant Kishor demolished the BJP’s 30-year hold on Bankipur, beating BJP’s Neeraj Kumar by over 19,000 votes, JD(U)’s Nitish Kumar met PM Modi at Parliament House, fuelling speculation over the NDA’s Bihar strategy ahead of state polls. Per India.com (Aug 4), Kishor said “the people voted against arrogance in Bankipur” and had “risen above caste considerations” in picking their representative.

stories.headline: Kerala Flood Toll Climbs to 20 as Red Alert Widens to Eight Districts
stories.body: Kerala’s monsoon disaster worsened with the death toll reaching 20 and five people still missing, as eight districts — including Pathanamthitta and Kottayam — were upgraded to red alert. Per Onmanorama (Aug 4), Thiruvarppu panchayat in Kottayam saw 98% of houses inundated after the river overflowed, exceeding 2018 flood levels, while roughly 13,500 people now shelter in 353 relief camps. Schools remain shut across ten districts as the IMD forecasts more heavy rain.

stories.headline: Apple Files Second UK Legal Challenge Over Secret iCloud Backdoor Order
stories.body: Apple has lodged a fresh complaint with the UK’s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, challenging a renewed government “technical capability notice” demanding backdoor access to encrypted iCloud backups. Per TechCrunch (Aug 3), this is Apple’s second fight over the issue — a similar 2025 order was dropped after pressure from the Trump administration — after Apple pulled its Advanced Data Protection feature for UK users in 2025 rather than comply. Apple has not commented publicly on the new challenge.

stories.headline: Reform UK’s Channel Navy Plan Mocked After Using Photo of a Ship Sold to Brazil
stories.body: Reform UK’s “Operation Fortress” policy document, unveiling plans to deploy the Royal Navy against Channel migrant boats, was undercut by its own cover image — a picture of HMS Ocean, which was sold to Brazil in 2018 and now serves as that country’s flagship. Per AOL UK (Aug 3), Conservative MP Ben Obese-Jecty quipped that Reform, “always across the detail on defence matters, have used a 2012 picture of HMS Ocean,” while former RAF commander Greg Bagwell dismissed the plan as “a complete word salad.” The blunder undercut Reform’s claims that senior ex-military figures had vetted the strategy.

stories.headline: New PM Andy Burnham Under Fire for Jetting Off on Holiday Two Weeks Into the Job
stories.body: Barely a fortnight after becoming Britain’s prime minister, Andy Burnham has drawn criticism for taking a working holiday abroad. Per The Spectator (Aug 5), Reform’s Lee Anderson accused him of “bunking off for a jolly abroad,” arguing Burnham “isn’t a prime minister that’s serious about leading,” while commentators noted the irony given Burnham had campaigned against “a revolving door of leaders.” Critics questioned whether he can tackle welfare reform, immigration and rough sleeping while working remotely from holiday.

stories.headline: Qatar Rejects ‘Politicising’ of Hormuz as Mediators Push for Short-Term Iran Deal
stories.body: Qatar reaffirmed its central mediating role in the Strait of Hormuz standoff, with government spokesperson Dr Majed Al-Ansari saying Doha maintains “intensive efforts and engagements with regional and international partners to prevent escalation,” working alongside Oman and Pakistan. Per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 5), Al-Ansari said Qatar “rejects the politicising of the Strait and its use as a means of pressure,” voicing hope mediation could unlock “a major deal that could help us walk back into a situation of peace in our region” — though no agreement has been finalised.

stories.headline: Amir, Trump Discuss Hormuz De-Escalation in Latest Phone Call
stories.body: Qatar’s Amir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani received a phone call from US President Donald Trump focused on easing US-Iran tensions and sustaining diplomatic momentum. Per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 4), Trump praised Qatar’s role “in supporting diplomatic efforts and facilitating dialogue between the parties,” while the Amir urged all sides to “adhere to what was agreed upon within the framework of the memorandum of understanding.”

stories.headline: UAE Revives Syria Business Council as DP World Pours $800 Million Into Tartus Port
stories.body: The UAE and Syria relaunched their joint business council to rebuild trade ties as Damascus recovers from war, with Essa Al Ghurair chairing the UAE side. Per The National (Aug 4), UAE Minister of Foreign Trade Dr Thani Al Zeyoudi cited the “desire of both countries to restore trade and investment relations to their full potential,” as Dubai’s DP World begins operations at Syria’s Tartus port with roughly $800 million in planned infrastructure upgrades.

doha_events.headline: Doha Gears Up to Host FIVB Boys’ U17 Volleyball World Championship
doha_events.body: Qatar will make history later this month as Doha hosts the 2026 FIVB Volleyball Boys’ U17 World Championship from Aug 19–29 — the country’s first-ever FIVB World Championship in any age or gender category. A field of 24 national teams is confirmed, and preparations are ramping up across the capital’s sporting venues, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 2).

doha_events.headline: ‘Layla and the Wolf’ Set to Enchant Young Audiences at THIS Theatre
doha_events.body: The Doha Players’ Arabic-language production “Layla and the Wolf” runs Aug 18–22 at THIS Theatre in Al Thumama, following a young girl’s magical visit to her grandmother and her encounter with a clever wolf. Aimed at children ages 4–11 and up, the five-session run teaches lessons on courage and trust, with tickets starting at QAR 65.

doha_events.headline: Tunisian Postal History Exhibition Still Drawing Visitors at Katara
doha_events.body: The exhibition of over 400 rare Tunisian postage stamps, dating from 1906 to 2010, remains open to visitors at the Museum of Arabic Postage Stamps in Building 22 at Katara Cultural Village. Curated around a teenage collector’s personal archive, the display traces cultural and historical milestones in Tunisia’s postal service, per Marhaba Qatar.

doha_events.headline: Msheireb Galleria’s ‘Aialna’ Back-to-School Checklist Lands Aug 20
doha_events.body: Msheireb Galleria’s back-to-school campaign “Aialna” kicks off Aug 20 and runs through the 29th, blending educational workshops, interactive activities, and rewards for families gearing up for the new school year, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 2). The event hasn’t started yet but stays on the calendar as one of August’s headline family happenings.

doha_events.headline: MIA’s ‘Family Day: The Life of Plants’ Blooms This Weekend
doha_events.body: The Museum of Islamic Art hosts a free family workshop, “Family Day: The Life of Plants,” on Saturday, Aug 8, from 2:30–4:30pm. The drop-in session explores plant symbolism in Islamic art through museum objects and hands-on activities, offered in both Arabic and English, per The Peninsula Qatar (Aug 5).
